llm.summary: The SKILL.md describes powerful Zero Trust hardening actions (firewall/egress changes, audits, apply/rollback) but the skill package contains no scripts or install steps and declares no credentials/dependencies — the pieces don't line up and require clarification before use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description claim a Zero Trust hardening framework that runs audit/harden/egress/verify workflows. The SKILL.md contains concrete shell commands and state file paths matching that purpose, but the actual skill bundle contains no script files or install spec — so the behavior described cannot be performed by the provided package as-is. That mismatch is a red flag (either the package is incomplete or it expects to fetch/assume external artifacts).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run specific shell scripts under /home/claw/.openclaw/workspace/skills/clawd-zero-trust/scripts/*, create/expect a compatibility symlink, modify egress/firewall state, and run verification checks against external providers (Telegram/GitHub/Anthropic/OpenAI). Those actions are within the stated scope (hardening/egress control) but they reference filesystem paths and system-modifying scripts that are not present in the package and may require additional privileges or credentials. The Plan-First principle is good, but the instructions give the agent direct commands to apply and rollback network-level changes — this needs explicit provenance and safety controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which typically lowers risk. However the SKILL.md references tooling and checks (shellcheck, quick_validate.py, package_skill.py) and expects scripts to exist under the skill directory. Because there are no code files provided and no documented install or download source, it's unclear how those scripts would be placed on disk; fetching arbitrary scripts from an unspecified source would be high risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill references external services (Tailscale, Telegram API, GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI) and transactional checks that imply network access and possibly credentials, but requires.env and primary credential are empty. No guidance is provided about what tokens/config are required or where they come from. That gap is disproportionate — either the skill will silently fail, or the missing credentials might be requested/used without clear declaration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (normal). The skill intends to create/maintain state under its skill directory (.state/egress-profile.json) and a compatibility symlink under workspace/scripts. Those are reasonable for a hardening tool, but they modify files in the agent's workspace and can persist firewall/egress state across runs. Because scripts are absent, it's unclear what will write/restore those files; users should expect persistent changes if the referenced scripts are later added or fetched.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run this skill as-is. The SKILL.md expects shell scripts and tooling that are not included in the package and does not declare required credentials — that mismatch is suspicious. Ask the publisher for: (1) the full source (scripts referenced under scripts/ and references/), (2) an install mechanism or trusted release URL and cryptographic checksums, (3) an explicit list of external dependencies and required environment variables/tokens (e.g., Telegram/Tailscale/OpenAI keys) and why each is needed, and (4) clear safety/rollback/testing instructions. Until you can verify the origin and review the actual scripts, consider running any hardening actions manually in a sandboxed test environment, or request a signed release artifact you can inspect before allowing the agent to execute apply/rollback commands.
